vqls-epsilon-definition: Section 2.1.1, p.3, Eq. (2): epsilon is defined as the trace distance between |x0> and |x(alpha_opt)>. The quote matches the definition.
vqls-cost-faithfulness-proof: Appendix B, p.11, and Section 2.1.2, p.3: (8) is proved in Appendix B from projector inequalities, then non-negativity and the vanishing condition follow. The full-rank (kappa finite) condition is stated. The paper writes 'A|x> = |b>' where its own text elsewhere says proportional; the value follows the paper's wording.
vqls-local-global-cost-bounds: Appendix B, p.11: both directions of (8) are proved. Lower bound from Pi_G >= Pi_L; upper bound from n Pi_L >= Pi_G by the bitstring-set argument (35). I checked the steps and they hold.
vqls-input-assumptions: Section 2.1.1, p.2: the paper states these assumptions on kappa, ||A|| and the unitaries A_l as its own input conditions.
vqls-input-form: Section 2.1.1, p.2: the paper states the input to VQLS as the gate sequence U and the decomposition (1) of A into L unitaries.
vqls-hadamard-overlap-test-properties: Appendix C.2, p.11: the paper defines the Hadamard-Overlap Test circuit (Fig. 9(b)) and states its resource use: one application each of U and V, uncontrolled, and 2n+1 qubits. This follows from the circuit as defined.
vqls-hadamard-overlap-real-part: Appendix C.2, p.12: Re[gamma] = 2(C(0) - C(1)) follows from (40) and (41). I checked the state after the final Hadamard and the SWAP expectation: the cross term gives exactly Re gamma. The paper says 'an explicit evaluation leads to' for (40) and (41), but the evaluation is routine and correct.
vqls-ansatz-fixed-structure-640-gates: Figure 3 caption, p.5: the paper states the size of its own ansatz (640 gates and 440 parameters for n = 50, four layers, linear scaling in n). Graded as the paper states it; I did not recount from the figure.
vqls-ising-optimizer-setup: Section 2.1.7, p.6: states the optimizer used for the Section 2.2.1 heuristics (random direction, line search).
vqls-random-matrix-optimizer-setup: Section 2.1.7, p.6: states that in Section 2.2.2 all parameters are independently optimized at each iteration.
vqls-opr-definition: Appendix G, p.15: the paper states the OPR definition it employs (taken from Ref. [60]) in its own words.
vqls-opr-global-cost-depolarizing: Appendix G.1, p.15: Eqs. (64) to (70) prove the argmin of the noisy normalized global cost equals the noiseless one. Assumptions (global depolarizing noise, equal effect on real and imaginary parts, layer counts independent of l, l') are stated and carried in the value. The proof is in the paper. Its modeling assumptions are the paper's own.
vqls-noise-models-limit: Appendix G, p.15 (also Section 2.1.8, p.6): the authors state they treat only simple noise models and leave more complicated ones for future work.
vqls-ising-qlsp-setup: Section 2.2.1, p.7: states J = 0.1 and the rescaling of zeta and eta so the smallest eigenvalue of A is 1/kappa and the largest is 1.
vqls-heuristics-no-finite-sampling: Section 2.2, p.7: states simulation without finite sampling and defines time-to-solution as the number of exact cost evaluations needed to guarantee epsilon below a value.
vqls-heuristics-epsilon-from-cost: Section 2.2, p.7: states the evaluation method (epsilon bounded via the cost and (9)) and that computing it from (2) would be 'essentially cheating'.
vqls-random-matrix-setup: Section 2.2.2, p.8: states four runs per random matrix, 10 random matrices, and time-to-solution as the average of the best run for each matrix.
vqls-hardware-setup-1024: Section 2.3, p.8: states the 10-qubit run on Rigetti 16Q Aspen-4, A of (26) with zeta = eta = 1, |b> = |0>, Ry ansatz, and the Pauli expansion of H_G for C_G.
vqls-finite-sampling-limit: Section 3, p.9: the authors state that the effect of finite sampling is not accounted for in their heuristics and remains to be seen. This is a caveat on the scope of their own results.
vqls-sparse-prefactor-limit: Appendix A, p.11: the authors state that the prefactor proportional to d forces precision inversely proportional to d, so the approach is only usable for sparse matrices with d much smaller than N. This is a limit on their own construction.
vqls-variable-ansatz-method: Appendix E, p.14: describes the paper's own variable-structure optimization (alternating inner and outer loops, random growth by identity-compiling gates), used for Section 2.2.2.
vqls-8x8-setup: Supplemental A.1, p.20: states A1, A2, A3 with degeneracy g = 1, 2, 4, 1000 runs per data point, and an ansatz with randomly initialized parameters (Fig. S1).
vqls-qaoa-setup-100-runs: Supplemental A.2, p.20: epsilon computed exactly, 100 runs per kappa with random parameters. I rendered page 20: the range is kappa = 10^0 to 10^3, so the value's 'powers of ten' reading is right.

theory_low.vqls-cost-lower-bound-theorem: Section 2.1.3, p.4: the proof step (13) uses E1 >= 1/kappa^2, 'which was shown in Ref. [8]'. A specific other paper's result is a step, so not a proved result in this paper. It also treats only the non-degenerate case and says the degenerate case 'works' without showing it.
theory_low.vqls-other-cost-bounds-follow: Section 2.1.3, p.4: one sentence says the remaining inequalities of (9) follow from (8) and <psi|psi> <= 1. They rest on the C_G >= eps^2/kappa^2 bound, which uses Ref. [8]'s E1 bound. The step <psi|psi> <= 1 is stated without proof. Not a stand-alone proved result.
theory_low.vqls-dqc1-hardness-proposition: Appendix D, p.13: the reduction rests on the DQC1-hardness of estimating Delta_HS and of Tr W from Ref. [33] ('it is known that ... is DQC1-hard [33]'). A specific other paper's theorem is the key step, so not a proved result in this paper.
theory_low.vqls-opr-local-cost-noise: Appendix G.2, p.16: the global depolarizing proof is in the paper, but it holds 'assuming the ansatz V(alpha) is capable of expressing the true solution', a condition the value drops. The measurement-noise claim is a remark ('we remark'), argued informally by treating symmetric measurement noise as a depolarizing channel, not proved. Two claims graded differently; graded by the weaker.
theory_low.vqls-sparse-decomposition-four-unitaries: Appendix A, p.10: the paper says the construction is 'from Ref. [8]' (Szegedy walks). Eq. (31) is stated with 'it follows that', without proof here. A cited construction, not proved in this paper.
theory_low.vqls-gradients-same-circuits: Appendix F, p.14: the global-cost gradients are derived via (55) to (62), but the local-cost gradients are only indicated ('a similar derivation can be used', Eq. (63) then 'hence'). The value covers both. The shifted-gate identity is also used without derivation. Graded by the weaker part.
